sources.title: Assessment of Microplastics in Fish GI Tracts and Shallow Water Sediments in Pugad Baboy Mangrove Area, Kawit, Cavite Using Fourier Transform Infrared-Attenuated Total Reflectance Spectroscopy
geographicScope: Pugad Baboy Mangrove Area, Kawit, Cavite
sources.accessStatus: Official publisher full text, PUPJST Volume 17 (2024), pages 25-44, read online on 2026-11-01 through the /article/download/50/26/101 route after the prior version route/article page failed in the earlier check. No local PDF retained.

fishSampleReview.sampling: The paper says three fish GI samples were taken from a local fishermen's catch on the sampling day in Pugad Baboy Mangrove; fish were 6.5-7.5 inches. The exact date and capture reach/station are not reported, and fish are not linked to one of the three sediment stations.
fishSampleReview.reportedIdentification: The fish are called spotted scat fish ('kitang') collectively. No scientific/binomial name, voucher accession, identification key, or specimen image suitable for taxonomic confirmation is reported.
fishSampleReview.studyResult: Two microplastic particles were isolated from the fish samples; the paper is a small method/pollution study, not a fish inventory or species-resolved ecological survey.
fishSampleReview.evidenceLimit: Retain as a historical common-name and local-catch lead only. Do not create a scientific species assertion, assign a specific capture station, infer salinity, or generalize current presence.

reuse.conclusion: Explicit noncommercial term retained. No unrestricted derived app-data approval is inferred.

salinityReview.reason: Mangrove/estuary wording alone does not prove measured salinity. The three fish are not linked to a sediment station or exact date, and the article provides no scientific name or voucher.
